arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Sinzdak argued the statute places the burden of proof on the asylum seeker.
She stated testimony must be persuasive and outweigh other evidence to meet that burden.
Mr. Katyal noted the government initially claimed courts should not enforce the presumption.
He argued the government now accepts the presumption applies in federal court reviews.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests how federal courts review asylum denials. The core dispute involves the legal weight of a credibility presumption. the sides that brought the case argue this presumption limits judicial review. the opposing sides argue courts must ignore it during substantial evidence checks.
